turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come in, sir. Err, your wife caught me outside only. She says the mole has turned almost black, it has bled quite a few times, and you have been dizzy with it.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): She wasn't asked. I am not dizzy. It bled once, once, and I am tired, so can we get on.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ah, sorry, this screen has frozen again. What did you say about the bleeding, say it once more?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Once. Last week it bled once, a little, then it stopped. She makes a drama.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. And the colour, she was telling nurse?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The colour has changed, yes, darker. Not jet black. Brown and a bit black, on my back, I can't even see it.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long is the mole itself there?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Two years. No, wait, before my son's wedding, that is four years. Four years it is sitting there.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, four? The system jumped. Four years?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, four years. The colour, she noticed it after Pune. Umm three weeks back... no, actually six weeks. Six weeks.
[SEG0011] person_1 (NURSE): Sir, vitals while you talk. Blood pressure one thirty six over eighty eight, pulse seventy eight, saturation ninety eight percent.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): One second, I didn't catch the pressure. Cursor was in the wrong box.
[SEG0013] person_1 (NURSE): One thirty six over eighty eight. Pulse seventy eight. Sats 98.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Is it paining? Any itch?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Not paining. It itches some nights, not every night. Irritating when I am trying to sleep.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Any loss of weight? I have to ask, you look worn out.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Weight is the same. I am worn out because I drive a taxi at night, not because of a mole.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Uh, your wife told the nurse you get dizzy. Say that again for me?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I said no. I am not dizzy. Don't write dizzy, I am just fed up and I want to go home and sleep.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any other skin trouble, rashes anywhere else?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only this one thing on the back.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sun, what about sun? You burn?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Badly. Since I was a boy in Kerala, every summer I was burnt. Even now if I am out without a shirt I burn easy.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicines? Any tablet daily?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Atorvastin for cholesterol. Seventy five milligrams... no, that is wrong, it is forty milligrams, at night. And I stopped the Shelcal, the calcium, two months back.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Forty milligrams at night, atorvastatin, yes. Shelcal stopped. Anything else, blood pressure tablet?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only that. And I don't smoke, if you are going to ask. I just want this finished.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look at the back. Shirt up. Left side, near the shoulder blade.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): It's cold in here. Just look and tell me, I'm half asleep.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Asymmetric, border not smooth. Colour is mixed brown and black. Diameter six millimetres... no, sorry, the scale says nine millimetres. No open sore today.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): So what is it? Don't give me a long lecture.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am concerned it is an atypical mole. I cannot rule out a melanoma, so that is not a final word, dermatology has to see it.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Melanoma. Fine. What do I do.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): I have booked the skin clinic, Tuesday week, that slot is fixed. And I will see you here in two weeks with the reports.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Two places. More waiting.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nurse will take bloods Thursday morning, full blood count and TSH, because of the tiredness. Come fasting, nothing to eat after midnight.
[SEG0037] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday morning bloods, I will put it in the book. Fasting.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): If those two are borderline we do ferritin, the third test. Only if borderline, not now.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): And the bleeding? It already stopped.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding does not settle before the skin clinic, we might do an ultrasound of that area. Not booked today.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): So I just wait and don't scratch it, is that the advice.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Don't scratch, don't pick, and keep the back covered in the sun. If it pours blood, press and go to emergency, but the Tuesday clinic stands.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I'm going. Tell my wife it is not an emergency tonight, she will be outside only, worrying.

spec.situation: Person with a mole on the back that partner says has changed in colour; bleeding once; sunburn history; doctor describes the mole by features and plans a dermatology referral.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Bleeding occurred once last week and stopped; not current.
bad.text: Mole bleeding (category=dermatological, status=present, temporality=current, body_site=back, reported_by=patient, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: Patient explicitly denies dizziness; nurse relayed wife's claim only.

omissions.text: Dizziness was explicitly denied by the patient twice ('I am not dizzy'); it should not be recorded as a present symptom.
Mole bleeding detail is incomplete/wrongly temporality-coded: the patient said it bled once only, last week, a little, then stopped.
No other daily tablets and no blood pressure tablet were denied by the patient.
